name: Archimedes Banya
priceLabel: $60 happy hour pass (weekday check-in 12:00–16:00, 3 h) · $72 basic pass, 3 h, any time · $95 all day
sauna: Two Russian saunas (parilki) at 170–210°F and 30–40% humidity, a Finnish dry sauna at 220°F and above, a Turkish hammam steam room below 140°F
pool: A cold water plunge, a warm swimming pool and jacuzzis
hours: Mon, Wed–Fri 12:00–23:00 · Sat–Sun 10:00–23:00 · last check-in 21:00, saunas and pool close 22:30 · Tuesdays only for the women's night (first Tuesday) and men's night (third Tuesday), 17:00–22:00
flag: 18 and over, with a government ID. A banya pass is required for entry. The banya floor is clothing optional after 18:00 every day and all day on Wednesdays and Fridays.
aufgussNote: Ask the room before adding steam in the Russian sauna; never water in the Finnish dry sauna. Staff also run a free aromatherapy Aufguss in the Russian sauna at 15:00, 19:00 and 21:00 (their home page adds 17:00 at weekends)

stove.note: Each Russian sauna is built around a 22,000 lb stove faced in handmade ceramic tiles from Russia

heatSrc: read off the venues' own pages, 25 Nov 2026

name: Kabuki Springs & Spa
priceLabel: $49 communal baths, 2½ h · 1½ h more for $25 · $20 with a treatment
sauna: A cedar-lined dry sauna heated to 150°F and an herbal steam room reaching 120°F, in a quiet communal Japanese-style bath
pool: A hot pool at 104°F and a cold plunge pool at 55°F
hours: Mon 14:00–20:00 · Tue–Sun 10:00–21:30 · baths by reservation only, in 2½-hour slots
flag: Women on Sun, Wed and Fri; men on Thu and Sat (bathing suit optional); all genders Mon and Tue, with bathing suits. Photo ID required. No walk-ins unless a reservation slot is free.

name: Alchemy Springs
priceLabel: Drop-in session, 2 h, from about $45 off-peak · most peak evenings and weekends from $75 · first-timer 2-pass $99
sauna: A social sauna at 180°F, a silent sauna at 185–200°F and an herbal steam room at 110–120°F, with an infrared-floored greenhouse to rest in
pool: A hot pool at 102–104°F and a cold plunge at 45–55°F
hours: Mon–Thu 16:00–22:00 · Fri 12:00–22:00 · Sat–Sun 10:00–20:00 · 2-hour sessions, a new group every 30 minutes
flag: Swimwear is required everywhere but the locker rooms, and phones stay in the locker. 18 and over. Walk-ins only when there is space; reservations open two weeks ahead and the price moves with demand.

stove.note: Two gas stoves heat the sauna. Its own site does not describe them

name: Onsen
priceLabel: $50 for 2 hours, with robe, towel and sandals
sauna: A redwood dry sauna and a steam room beside a communal soaking tub
pool: A 104°F communal soaking tub and an overhead cold plunge
hours: Mon 16:00–22:00 (men) · Wed 14:00–18:00 (women), 18:00–22:00 co-ed · Thu 14:00–22:00 · Fri–Sun 10:00–22:00 · no Tuesday hours listed
bestFor: Small sento-style soak with a restaurant
flag: Monday is men only and Wednesday 14:00–18:00 women only, both bathing suit optional; a bathing suit is required at all co-ed times. 18 and over, four guests at most per reservation.

name: Dogpatch Paddle
priceLabel: $25 sauna only, 1 h, shared with up to three others · $35 with the cold plunge · private $100 / $140
sauna: A waterfront sauna kept at about 190°F, four people at most
pool: A cold plunge kept at about 49°F (36–55°F), with the beach right outside
hours: Tue–Sun 09:00–17:00, last public sauna 16:00 · closed Mon · one-hour sessions
bestFor: An hour of hot and cold by the water
flag: 16 and over. Public sessions run 9 to 5; members get 07:30–21:00.

name: Fjord
priceLabel: $45 shared session, 90 min · private sauna $270 for 2 h, up to 6 guests
sauna: Two traditional Finnish-style saunas kept at a target of 190°F, six people each, on a floating platform in a marina
pool: No pool: you plunge in the Bay inside a marked zone, or cool off under the outdoor showers
hours: Open daily 08:00–20:30, Tuesdays 14:00–20:30 · sessions are booked ahead; the calendar opens Sundays at 09:00 with a new week, two weeks out
bestFor: Sauna and a plunge in the Bay
flag: Bathing attire is required at all times. Bring at least two towels, water and footwear. No soap in the showers. Minimum age 14, with an adult in the group. Free Open Access sessions run every two weeks.
aufgussNote: Löyly is allowed: pour small amounts of water over the hot stones
heatSrc: read off the venues' own pages, 25 Nov 2026

name: Albany Sauna
priceLabel: $30 for 30 min, one person · 45 min $45, or $70 for two · 60 min $60, or $85 for two · each further person $25
sauna: Four private sauna rooms sharing one central brick furnace filled with several tons of river rocks, built in 1934; each room seats up to four
pool: No pool: water buckets and an overhead waterfall above the bench, and a shower in each room. The outdoor hot tubs are under construction
hours: The sauna opens every day from 12:00, last appointment 21:00 · by reservation, with a signed waiver
bestFor: A private room where you make your own steam
flag: Reservations by phone or text, not online. Staff show first-timers how to work the damper and the water valve: the four rooms share one furnace, so steam you make reaches the others. Towels are included. An older hours block on the same site lists other times; the sauna page and the booking notice agree on the ones given here.
aufgussNote: You open the damper for heat and pull the water valve to put water on the rocks inside the furnace. Wait at least 30 seconds between pulls, because the steam reaches all four rooms

stove.note: One central brick furnace holding several tons of river rocks, gas-fired for five hours each morning and then shut with the chimney closed, so the rocks stay hot through the day

heatSrc: read off the venues' own pages, 25 Nov 2026

name: Good Hot
priceLabel: $30 a seat in the quiet communal sauna (first and last slots on Mon, Thu and Fri, first slot at weekends) · private sauna $130 for 1½ h, up to 6 people · $150 for the two larger ones, up to 8 · $20 off on Mon and Thu
sauna: Five small saunas rented privately and a communal one with six seats, on the shore at Terminal 4; the heat is adjustable up to about 180°F
pool: No pool: a small beach beside the saunas for a plunge in the Bay, and two cold rinse showers
hours: Thu–Mon, generally 09:30–20:15 · closed Tue–Wed · by reservation only, up to 21 days ahead
bestFor: A private sauna and a dip in the Bay
flag: No drop-in bathing: every visit is booked, and the gate code and directions come with the confirmation. 18 and over, no dogs. Wear swimsuit bottoms or a wrap outside the saunas. Sandals or water shoes are required for the water, which is out of reach at very low tide.
aufgussNote: Guests are asked not to add water to the rocks: the heaters are sensitive to water

stove.note: Commercial heaters that take no water on the rocks
